name: Palingenetic ultranationalism
summary: Roger Griffin's term for what he takes to be the minimum of generic fascism: an ultranationalism built on the myth that a decadent nation will be reborn through a revolution that sweeps away the liberal, socialist and conservative old order. It mobilizes the people as a unified mass under a new elite and sometimes a heroic leader, treats violence as part of renewal, and is anti-liberal, anti-Marxist and anti-conservative. Economics, leadership forms and racial doctrine vary by movement and are not part of the core.
scope: Roger Griffin's palingenetic ultranationalism: his 'fascist minimum', the claim that generic fascism is a populist ultranationalism whose mythic core is the rebirth (palingenesis) of a nation held to be in decline, as set out in The Nature of Fascism (1991) and his later restatements (the 1996 'Staging the Nation's Rebirth' chapter and its retrospective, the German article 'Palingenetischer Ultranationalismus'), and as summarised in the European Center for Populism Studies glossary. Economic, institutional and racial positions that Griffin treats as contingent are not part of the core. The Doctrine of Fascism (1932) is not tied to this subject by any defining source (they name Griffin's definition, not that text), so it is not a source for it; the same goes for the general Wikipedia article on fascism. Excludes postwar neo-fascism and non-fascist authoritarian nationalism (para-fascism), which Griffin separates from the minimum.
